text:
The most interesting man in this building may be the one who has not played lately. Ottawa sent Jonas Johansson to the AHL, which, as The Athletic's Julian McKenzie put it, clears the way for Linus Ullmark's return. In eight games Ullmark has been superb: .945, 8.2 goals saved above expected. That is a sharp turn from last season, when he finished 13.3 goals below expected in 49 games. Samuel Ersson has carried the load in between, and Ottawa now has a goalie decision that feels like a good problem.

Colorado arrives after putting six on Toronto on Tuesday. The Avalanche score 4.11 goals a game, and the honest read is that some of that is hot hands: a +20 goal difference on +12.4 expected, with finishing 12.7 goals above what their chances usually produce. The process is still very good (53% of the five-on-five expected goals, and a penalty kill allowing only 0.56 expected goals a game). Cale Makar got through an injury scare and was good to go Tuesday. Devon Toews may be the quiet story of their season: 11 points in his last ten, earned on more chances of his own (2.1 expected goals on his shots against a usual 1.3).

The Senators are 3-1-1 in their last five with 59% of the expected goals, the best process of anyone in this game lately. They are doing it without William Eklund (ankle, out until January), with Tim Stützle sliding beside Dylan Cozens and Jesper Zetterlund. Nick Cousins is out at least a week after a hit from Jakob Chychrun, per Daily Faceoff, and Andre Burakovsky and Warren Foegele are also missing. Ottawa takes 4.7 penalties a game, which is the one habit you would not want against Nathan MacKinnon on the top power play.

Small milestones on both benches: Artem Zub plays his 400th NHL game, Philip Tomasino is one point from 100, and Parker Kelly is one goal from 50 against a former team. Our numbers make it close: Colorado 3.04 expected goals, Ottawa 2.93.
headline: Ullmark's return meets the Avalanche's finishing
